correctness.rationale: Every fort is decomposed by its selected original vertices and underlying selected edges. Crossing-edge constraints and the absence of degree-one outside original vertices force inclusion-minimal forts to be precisely all originals, one star-type fort per original vertex, or an edge-only simple-cycle fort. Direct fort–forcing obstruction equivalence then gives the forest/singleton characterization. The subset sum is exactly the graphic matroid forest expansion of T(1+z,1) with n exceptional stars removed. Cayley's formula gives the leading nonzero coefficient. The independent brute-force forcing/fort checker reproduces all coefficients for n=3,4,5; n=6 has 25,000 seeded trials. Finite trials are not the all-n proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 complete-subdivision paper determines the zero forcing number but not the full forcing-set distribution. The 2018 zero forcing polynomial and 2024 graph-operation papers do not state the full-subdivision K_n enumeration in the inspected sections. The 2023 fort article supplies general fort methods but not this explicit hypergraph and graphic-matroid characterization. Searches of the published mathematical research collection under exact and equivalent descriptions returned unrelated family-specific forcing and fort findings. A hidden equivalence in more general graph-subdivision/graphic-matroid literature is the main residual originality risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed older graph subdivision theorems or matroid-transversal identities may already yield the full characterization in equivalent language.

value.rationale: The full exact cardinality enumerator refines a previously known extremal scalar and reveals a natural graphic-matroid/Tutte-polynomial structure; the simple-cycle and star taxonomy of every minimal obstruction is the structural mechanism, not a numerical reparameterization. It simultaneously enumerates all ordinary forcing sets and a nontrivial class of minimum sets for all graph orders n≥3, with future utility for coefficient inequalities, random initial sets, and related fort hypergraphs.
